findings.highlight: call for the one who can beat her!
findings.evidenceJa: こいつに勝てる[ruby text=セイバー char=2]存在を呼び寄せるしかない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou must summon the “existence” capable of defeating Rider, explicitly read as “Saber.”
findings.explanation: The English keeps an unnamed “one” but omits the written existence/Saber reading relation at the moment he considers Command Spell summoning.

findings.governingReading: Shirou hears a splashing, surging sound like blood flowing.
findings.explanation: The English turns the simile into an assertion that the audible substance is blood.

findings.highlight: I feel pain from my left hand.
findings.evidenceJa: 痛みと、左手から激しい痛み。
findings.governingReading: Sound, pain, and then another surge of intense pain from the left hand overlap.
findings.explanation: The English collapses the repeated escalation into one generic pain statement.

findings.highlight: I see that my left arm is cut from my elbow. The Command Spells are fading, and my arm
findings.evidenceJa: 令呪の薄れゆく、俺の、腕
findings.governingReading: Shirou sees his arm as the Command Spell fades; the Japanese withholds a complete syntactic description through his scream.
findings.explanation: The English inserts a declarative elbow amputation absent from this active line, then leaves the actual source fragment dangling after “my arm.”

findings.highlight: My vocal organs appeal to me about the pain.
findings.evidenceJa: 発声器官は俺のモノではなくなったように、耐え難い痛みをひたすらに訴える。
findings.governingReading: As though no longer belonging to Shirou, his vocal organs do nothing but cry out the unbearable pain.
findings.explanation: The English awkwardly makes the organs appeal to Shirou and omits bodily alienation, intolerability, and relentless expression.

findings.highlight: You are only a person who binds the Servant using your Command Spell.
findings.evidenceJa: 令呪によってサーヴァントを律するだけの人間です
findings.governingReading: Rider calls Shirou merely another human who governs or compels a Servant through Command Spells.
findings.explanation: “Binds” blurs command authority into physical or contractual binding and weakens Rider’s accusation about coercive control.

findings.highlight: if there’s a wound this big
findings.evidenceJa: 肘の先からまるごと、バケツめいた孔が出来たら
findings.governingReading: A bucket-like hole has taken away the arm wholesale beyond the elbow.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the exact catastrophic anatomy and bucket image to a generically large wound.

findings.highlight: To make you use your Command Spell
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方に令呪を使わせるこの狩りの中で
findings.governingReading: Within this hunt designed to force Shirou to use a Command Spell, Rider set herself conditions.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the objective but omits Rider’s explicit framing of the encounter as a hunt.

findings.highlight: I will orgasm if I gouge your eyes out as well.
findings.evidenceJa: 間違いなく達してしまいますから
findings.governingReading: Rider says she would undoubtedly “reach it” or climax, using indirect language whose sexual meaning is carried by the surrounding sadistic satisfaction.
findings.explanation: The English states “orgasm” outright, collapsing the euphemistic mechanism and making an implied sexual reading explicit fact.

findings.evidenceJa: ほんとうに出血で[line4]んでしまうマえに
findings.governingReading: Before Shirou truly dies from blood loss, he tries to form a final decision about Saber.
findings.explanation: The English retains imminent death but omits blood loss as its specific cause.

findings.highlight: I would have extracted your heart, gouged out your chest, but I shall restrain myself
findings.evidenceJa: 本来なら胸を抉って息の根を止めますが
findings.governingReading: Rider says she would ordinarily gouge out Shirou’s chest to stop his life or breath.
findings.explanation: The English exposes competing conditional variants, adds heart extraction, and then also prints the chest-gouging rendering in the same sentence.

findings.highlight: You shall survive if you are lucky
findings.evidenceJa: 運が良ければ助かるでしょうが
findings.governingReading: If Shirou is lucky, he may survive until Rin arrives.
findings.explanation: “Shall survive” turns Rider’s probabilistic forecast into an assurance conditioned only on luck.

findings.highlight: Saber. I… have… to call… Saber
findings.evidenceJa: セイバー。俺は、セイバーを、呼ばない、と
findings.governingReading: Shirou forms the decision that he will not call Saber, despite dying suspended in the trap.
findings.explanation: The English reverses refusal into obligation, erasing the defining choice not to compel Saber and changing the death branch’s characterization and causal meaning.

findings.highlight: You have fulfilled me enough with your voice of anguish.
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方の苦悶の声だけで十分すぎるほど満たされた。
findings.governingReading: Rider reports that Shirou’s anguished voice alone has satisfied her more than enough.
findings.explanation: “You have fulfilled me” awkwardly makes Shirou the grammatical fulfiller and weakens Rider’s controlled self-report of sadistic satisfaction.

findings.highlight: I have to call for Saber… with my Command Spell…
findings.governingReading: Through the Command Spell, Saber…; Shirou’s cognition fails on an unfinished object marker before he can complete the thought.
findings.explanation: The English supplies a coherent obligation and completed action, removing the syntactic collapse that distinguishes this dying thought from a resolved command.

findings.evidenceJa: 胸を抉って息の根を止めますが
findings.governingReading: Rider says she would gouge open Shirou’s chest in order to stop his breath and end his life.
findings.explanation: Even the closer conditional branch omits the attack’s explicitly stated lethal purpose, leaving only mutilation.

findings.highlight: your brain will not function even if you are saved.
findings.evidenceJa: もう脳はまともに機能しないでしょうね
findings.governingReading: Rider predicts that Shirou’s brain will probably no longer function normally or properly even if he survives.
findings.explanation: The English omits まともに and strengthens the prediction into categorical total nonfunction.
